known_issues: Real flat floods still look fairly flat in 3D. St. Johns River and Calcasieu River open at ×10 and the key says 'Still flat at ×10: raise it, or use River view.' (×15 and ×20 are offered). The demo flood shows the effect clearly; real floods only modestly.

On real floods the grey 'no satellite view' hatching covers much of the 3D view (St. Johns River passes are 53 to 97 % hidden by clouds or missing data), and the depth tint shows only where a pass saw water: small patches at Calcasieu, little at St. Johns.
Height above the river tints almost all land on flat coastal plains (Calcasieu, St. Johns), so it adds little there. It is off by default and labelled 'Not a flood map'.

Depth estimates are rough: a little low near gentle banks, a metre or more off where banks are steep or the water map and terrain do not line up, and near 0 m in the river's normal channel. Depth exists only for the bundle's shown pass, each kept pass and the NWS forecast area; a pass shown only as its picture has no depth surface (the key says so).

At a past step the NWS forecast flooded area, FEMA, NWS category maps and the model still show now (tagged 'now'), and 'Official now' lists what is in effect now; the step's own NWS versions are in the 'NWS · n' list and on the map.

At now the map draws the pass the satellite layer picked (shown_key), which can be older than the newest usable pass (St. Johns: Oct 26 shown, Oct 29 listed). The 3D key says 'Newer satellite passes exist'; the 2D legend does not. A later brief could let shown_key prefer the newest usable pass.

NASA lists a satellite pass 2 to 4 days after it was taken, so the newest days of a live flood often have no step yet ('No satellite image after Oct 29 yet'). The radar route (DSWx-S1, EARTHDATA_TOKEN) is tested offline only; no token was set here.

user_summary:
Brief 6 is finished and checked. Here is what changed, in plain words.

The new name
- The app is now called Disaster Mapping everywhere you see it: the logo and name in the top bar, the browser tab title, every message, and the README, which is rewritten for a fires-and-floods app. On narrow screens and in Forensic the bar shows only the logo, but the name stays in the tab title and for screen readers.
- Things you never see keep their old code names on purpose, so your settings, your .env file, your data/ folder and old links keep working: for example the fire3d Python package and the FIRE3D_ settings.
- Floods you prepared before today may still show "Fire-3d" in a saved note (for example the satellite login note in Forensic) until you prepare them again. The README's Known limits section gives the commands. The floods in this cloud copy are already clean.

"Why can't I have flood animation? Is there no data?"
- There is data, but it comes in separate snapshots, not as a film. A satellite photographs a place only every few days, and NASA lists each picture 2 to 4 days late. The National Weather Service (NWS) issues, updates and ends its warnings at particular moments.
- So flood "animation" now steps through those real moments. Open a flood in Command (or Forensic) and look above the river-level chart at the bottom. A row reads, for example, "3 satellite passes and 1 NWS product change from Oct 25 · Play steps through them".
- Press Play (or the Space key) to step through them one by one, every couple of seconds. The arrow buttons, or the comma and full stop keys, go one step back or forward. Play never starts by itself, and it stops at the latest step. If your computer is set to reduce motion, each press shows just one step.
- At each step the map shows that satellite picture with its own date and age ("Satellite pass Oct 29 · 7 days before now · no view of 61% of the area"). Grey hatching marks where clouds or missing data hid the ground. The map also shows the NWS warning areas that were in effect at that time.
- Nothing is invented between two pictures. Between passes the row says which picture is shown and how old it is ("Shown: satellite image of Oct 29 (6 days before the handle) · No satellite image after Oct 29 yet").
- At a past step, the small "NWS · 1" button lists the warnings drawn at that time. Each keeps its issuer, its own times, NWS's own words and a link; older copies from the Iowa Environmental Mesonet archive are marked "archived copy".
- Layers that only describe now (the NWS forecast area, FEMA, the model) stay on screen and are tagged "now". The Public view has no time steps: it always shows now.

"Forensic in floods is flat and we can't see the affected areas. What's the fix?"
Four things were added to the 3D flood view:
- River view: a flood now opens in a lower, closer look along its main river. The "River view" button brings it back, and "Frame flood" still shows the whole area.
- Height boost: on flat land, heights are drawn several times taller, so low ground and banks show. The amount is worked out automatically from how flat the area is, and it is always on screen (for example "Height ×10 · auto" in the bottom bar). You can choose another value there, from ×1 to ×20. Distances stay true; only heights are stretched.
- Estimated depth: inside water that was actually mapped (by the satellite, or NWS's forecast flooded area), a see-through water surface is tinted by how deep the water might be: deeper is darker blue. The depth is estimated from the height of the ground along the water's edge (a published method called FwDET). It is labelled experimental: it can be off by a metre or more, and it is never drawn where no water was mapped.
- Height above the river ("low ground"): off by default. Turn it on in Layers → From the terrain. It tints land 0–1 m, 1–2 m and 2–5 m above the nearest river channel, worked out from the terrain alone. It shows low ground near rivers, not where water is: it is labelled "Not a flood map".
- Play and the step buttons also work in the Forensic dock. The 3D satellite picture, its depth surface and the NWS warning lines change with each step.

Honest result:
- On the demo flood (a hilly made-up valley), the change is clear.
- On real flat floods (St. Johns River in Florida, Calcasieu River in Louisiana), it helps, but those places still look fairly flat even at ×10. The key says "Still flat at ×10: raise it, or use River view."
- On those real floods, clouds and missing data hide a large part of most satellite pictures, so the grey hatching dominates and the depth tint shows only in small patches.
- On a wide flat coastal plain, the height-above-the-river layer tints almost everything, so it adds little there.
- An untinted area, a shallow depth or a dry pixel is never an all-clear.

Zoom dimming
- The darkening of the map's edges as you zoom in (the "globe" look) is now off by default.
- To turn it on, open Layers & settings (the layers button at the top right), go to Display and switch on "Zoom dimming". Your choice is remembered in this browser.

How it was checked
- All automatic tests pass: backend 1466; web 1917, with 2 data tests skipped and the lint warnings unchanged at 55. The app builds.
- I took 27 final screenshots and looked at each one: both overviews, fire and flood views in all three workspaces, time steps in Command and Forensic, 3D before/after on the demo flood and two real floods, dimming off and on, and phones.
- An automated browser run passed 134 of 134 checks. On every view: the old name never appears, the new name is in the title, "Research prototype — not for operational use" and "Not an all-clear. Follow local officials." are visible, and there are no errors. It also checked that Play, Pause and the keys work, that nothing plays by itself, and that the dimming switch works and is remembered.
- The fire views look the same as before apart from the name and the dimming default.
- Scans found no secret keys in the code or its history, no "FireTrace", and no "safe" or "low risk" in the app's wording.

What is left (small)
- The 2D map does not yet say when a newer satellite picture exists than the one it shows at now; the 3D key does.
- Forensic's credits outside the bottom dock do not yet name the Iowa Environmental Mesonet archive when archived warnings are drawn; the dock does.
- Forensic was only tested with software graphics in the cloud. Please open a fire and a flood in Forensic on your Mac once to confirm that it looks right on a real graphics card.
- To try the demo flood, run `uv run python scripts/make_fixture.py --only flood` and then `uv run python scripts/flood_3d.py fixture-flood` (both from backend/). The README shows this.
